audit_target.question: are the boundary verdicts of the raw 0F 05 candidate scan reproducible from the bytes, and is every valid entry a real instruction start

second_decoder.banner: GNU objdump (Binutils for MinGW-W64 x86_64, built by Brecht Sanders, r4) 2.47.20260726

method: own byte census over every raw backed section
own exception directory parse with ordering, overlap and emptiness validation
own Capstone linear sweep of every owning runtime function
own recursive descent seeded with every runtime function entry
GNU objdump linear disassembly of the same ranges as the second decoder
not_performed: the specimen is never mapped for execution and no module is loaded
the audited script is never executed and the audited CSV is never written
no service number is decoded and no Nt/Zw service name is asserted
no caller, argument dataflow or intent classification is attempted

audited_script.note: 3881 is the raw hit count of the scope section, not a line count of the audited script

audited_csv.rdata_data: absent, the CSV scope is the executable section only

instruction_start_validation.claim_under_test: a raw byte pair is a real instruction only when it is an instruction start on a decoded executable path, and the only path the audited script decodes is the linear sweep of the owning runtime function

second_decoder.role: decoder that shares no code with either implementation

definition.fallthrough_proven: on an uninterrupted fallthrough chain from the owning function entry, so the instruction start follows from the entry alone
definition.branch_proven: not on the fallthrough chain, but a resolvable direct branch of the same function reaches the address in the recursive descent
definition.sweep_hypothesis: only the linear sweep reaches the address, which requires the decode to continue across a control transfer the sweep ignores

recursive_descent.seeds: every runtime function entry of the exception directory

instruction_start_validation.verdict: every valid entry is an instruction start of its owning runtime function under two independent decoders, so none of them is a decoder artifact; the proof level split states how far each start is control flow proven

notes: no owner function needed a stopped sweep, so no candidate is left undecided by an undecodable byte inside its own runtime function
no direct branch target lands inside another instruction, so no candidate is entered through a mid instruction transfer
the pdata gap entries stop being ambiguous once the descent is added: none is an instruction start reachable from any runtime function entry
a hypothesis only entry is not a defect of the audited script, whose docstring states the linear sweep as the decode channel; it is a limit of what the evidence file alone can prove

false_positive_explanations.definition: why a raw byte pair is not a syscall instruction, grouped by the channel that decides it

channel_reasons.covered_by_instruction: the byte pair is an interior byte of the preceding instruction, so it is consumed as an opcode, a displacement or an immediate by that instruction and is never decoded
channel_reasons.no_pdata_function: no runtime function covers the rva, so the sweep has no decode context and no instruction start can be asserted for the byte pair
channel_reasons.non_executable_section: the owning section carries neither IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE nor IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE, so the byte pair can never be executed as an instruction

provenance_method.reported: the shape of the last RAX definition only, never a value

provenance_classes.constant_immediate_in_window: an immediate reaches RAX inside the window, so the number is a build time constant on that path
provenance_classes.register_or_memory_derived_in_window: the last RAX definition in the window reads a register, memory or an arithmetic result, so the number is path dependent there
provenance_classes.no_eax_definition_in_window: no RAX definition inside the window, so the number is defined further up or on another path
